# **Communication plan** 

Main & Backup Channels  
Our main channel will be Instagram. It will be used for project communication, including organising meetings, notifying members about project updates and answering questions. Our backup channel will be email. This will be used when a member cannot be reached through the main channel or if Instagram is temporarily unavailable.

Expected response times  
Team members are expected to acknowledge project messages through the main channel within 24 hours. Members are not expected to be continuously available. If someone knows they will be unavailable for an extended period, they should notify the team beforehand where possible.

Meeting schedule/format  
The team will meet twice in person weekly on Tuesday 11am \- 2pm and Thursday 2pm \- 4pm. The meetings will cover progress since the last meeting, decisions that need to be made, problems that occurred, allocation of responsibilities and actions to be completed before the next meeting. Additional meetings will be arranged when/if required. If a member cannot attend a scheduled meeting, they should notify the group beforehand and provide an update on their assigned work where possible.

How decisions get made  
The team will aim to make decisions through open discussion and consensus. Members should explain their reasoning behind opinions on the task.  Where a consensus cannot reasonably be reached, the team will use a majority vote.

How you'll use GitHub to manage work  
GitHub will be the team’s main system for managing and tracking project work. Tasks will be created as GitHub issues, which will have a clear description and an assigned team member. 

# **Conflict resolution plan** 

## What we consider a conflict

A project issue may be treated as a conflict when it begins to negatively affect another member or the team’s ability to complete work. A single mistake or unavoidable delay will not automatically be considered a conflict. The team will consider the circumstances and focus first on solving the problem. 

Conflicts include repeatedly failing to respond to team communication, regularly missing meetings without communication, failing to complete agreed work without warning, making significant project changes without consulting team members and disrespectful communication.

## Raising an Issue

The person affected should raise the issue respectfully with the member concerned and should focus on what has occurred, how it affects the team and what actions are needed to resolve the issue.

## Internal Resolution Process

If the issue cannot be resolved through conversation between the two members, then the rest of the team will be informed and included in the discussion. A whole team discussion will be held where the members can explain their perspectives and as a group will agree on specific actions required to resolve the issue.
